name: Nikolay Petrushev
strengths: Petrushev takes a deep kick-slide at 6-6 and locks the rusher out so the arc has to go around his length.
Petrushev latches in the run game, washes a tackle inside, then climbs and swallows the linebacker.
Petrushev plays both edges as 78 — same length set at left tackle and right tackle.
weaknesses: Petrushev’s pad level stays high, and he will bend at the waist instead of sinking — elite speed can win the edge until the hips drop.
comparison: Petrushev comps to Wyatt Milum — 6-6 tackle mold with length to mirror the edge and a 285 frame still filling toward starter mass.
projection: Petrushev projects as a Year 1 develop, Year 2–3 rotation OT. Ceiling: multi-year SEC starter if 285 becomes mass and the pad level comes down.
schemeFit: Petrushev fits a developmental boundary OT — length to protect the edge first, mass and pad level still catching the 6-6 frame.
